title: Sharp Regret for Median-Based Treatment Choice at Quadratic Density Zeros
banked_reason: Supervisor stop: capped D-stage proposal after three REVISEs; recurring exact-zero applicability objection, not a mathematical refutation. An exact density zero with quadratic order at every arm-specific conditional median and every covariate is destroyed by arbitrarily small measurement error; the radial synthetic witness establishes nonemptiness but not realistic applicability of this load-bearing model.
gap_reasons: An exact density zero with quadratic order at every arm-specific conditional median and every covariate is destroyed by arbitrarily small measurement error; the radial synthetic witness establishes nonemptiness but not realistic applicability of this load-bearing model.
proof_attempt_summary: Three field-tier REVISEs prompted comparator, assumption-tagging, witness, and scope repairs. The last review retained only the exact-zero applicability objection. Supervisor ordered give-up at the D-stage cap; no claim was mathematically refuted and no Lean proof was delivered. A positive-floor or measurement-error primary model would require a new research question.
tldr: The exact quadratic median-density zero is a stress-test model for ACME treatment choice at fitted conditional-outcome valleys. The headline question determines sharp original-record regret on the fixed primitive full-density class, including every necessary logarithm, an attaining rule and a same-class all-policy converse. Reciprocal derivative smoothing and normalized moving-zero testing are concrete handles. Three outcome derivatives and the uniform mixed restrictions are newly maintained; a fourth outcome derivative would change the class. A signed three-shock norm supplies a legal generative witness. A separate quantitative measurement-noise theorem determines the induced positive floor, inverse-CDF crossover, original-target regret sensitivity and ACME target drift. ACTG 175 supplies the published median-choice workflow only, with no evidence of an exact zero and no value-coverage claim.
gap: Regular ACME scores divide by conditional median density. Stoye's finite-sample mean-welfare result permits unrestricted cross-covariate variation, while Chen et al.'s joint \(BC^4\) theory concerns derivative roots. Neither determines sharp smooth conditional-median regret with exact quadratic zeros and fixed mixed-derivative budgets. Positive-floor interpolation is a separate problem.
fill: The sharp-regret question derives the numerical minimax sequence and a total original-data learner with a normalized full-class converse. Supporting bias and covariance lemmas use the stipulated three derivatives. A separate convolution theorem gives a uniform positive-floor inverse modulus and bounds changes in original-target policy regret and ACME value; it delineates the stress test without promising positive-floor minimax adaptation.
